name: Shakti septal ('pleasure center') signal, coils front to back
summary: Murphy's Shakti septal signal from two still coils in a front-to-back line on the midline behind the top of the head, over the upper parietal strip. The vendor presents it for pleasant and sexual sensations; the reported after-effects are two user testimonials. The waveform is rebuilt from the vendor's only description, 'very low frequencies'.
setting: Quiet room, eyes closed, relaxed. Only two coils, one behind the other on the midline: CPz, a little behind the top of the head, and Pz behind it; the other six stay unused.
schedule: At most weekly; the vendor warns not to over-use it.
notes: The vendor shows this arrangement as a picture and gives one sentence on the place: the upper part of the parietal strip, 'located from an inch behind the very top of the head to two inches from that point' (septum_consent.htm). This program plays 20 min on two still coils, one behind the other on the midline: CPz and Pz, both with the same signal. Both lie inside the strip, which begins about an inch behind Cz, the very top of the head. The site names are this project's reading of that sentence (an inch taken as 2.5 cm, Cz to CPz as about 3.5 cm). The 20 min are this project's choice. The vendor's file is not published; it says only that the signal has 'very low frequencies' and 'requires a higher volume than the others' (septum_consent.htm, Important note). The stand-in is this project's amygdala stand-in slowed down: a rising sweep from 1 to 6 Hz, 230 points of 3 ms (0.69 s), then 4 s of silence. Side by side: murphy-shakti-septal-horizontal. Field strength: the vendor gives sound-card volume settings only (65% for men and 42% for women on a PCI card, 100% and 85% otherwise). The 1 uT default is this project's. This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. The effect rests on two user testimonials on the vendor's site, which adds: 'This signal is not a treatment for any medical condition' (pleasure_center.htm). One vendor page says the signal was 'tested with only a few human and no animal subjects' (septum_consent.htm); two others say 'It has not been tested with human or animal subjects' (sexual_effects.htm; 8_coil_septal_consent.htm). Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). The brain view has no septal region, so no target is highlighted. Not for people with epilepsy; stop if it is unpleasant.
source: Murphy, Shakti and the brain's pleasure center – the septum https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/pleasure_center.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Septum signal https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/septum_consent.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: Sexual effects https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/winshakti/demo/shakti_demo/sexual_effects.htm ; Murphy, Shakti demo: What are 'Rapid' and 'High-Speed' signals?
